title: Michail Antonio says he is ‘praying for peace’ after Al Sailiya move confirmed
content:
Former West Ham United forward Michail Antonio said he is “praying that God brings peace to the whole region” after his move to Qatari side Al Sailiya was confirmed.

Antonio, 35, has been without a club since the Premier League team decided in August not to offer him a new contract, bringing an end to his 10-year spell with them.

The forward had not played for the London side since December 2024, after he was involved in a single-vehicle collision when his car struck a tree in Epping Forest. He underwent surgery on a lower limb fracture and missed the remainder of the season. His contract was due to expire in June but West Ham said they would delay their decision over his contract until a “right and appropriate” time after his “unique” situation and he played two under-21 games for them that August.

Qatar has been affected by escalating conflict in the Middle East after strikes from the United States and Israel on Iran, and its government said on Monday that its air force had shot down two Iranian bomber jets.

The Jamaica international referenced the conflict in a post on his Instagram account after his move was confirmed by the Qatari side on Monday.

“First and foremost, I’m praying that God brings peace to the whole region and around the world and keeps everyone safe,” he said. “I’m grateful for the opportunity to step back onto the pitch when the time is right and do what I love.”

Al Sailiya are 10th of 12 clubs in the Qatar Stars League after 16 games.

After Antonio’s West Ham departure, then-Leicester head coach Marti Cifuentes, who left the side in January, said to the BBC in December that Antonio had been training with the Championship club. Cifuentes said there were no signs of ill effect from Antonio’s injury, and that match fitness would take “some time” due to the forward being “away for a long period”.

Antonio returned to the pitch for Jamaica in June, making three substitute appearances as his side — then led by Steve McClaren — suffered a group-stage exit in the Gold Cup. He was also called up to the Jamaica squad for September’s World Cup qualifiers, but was an unused substitute and was not picked for Jamaica’s October and November squads.

Jamaica will take on New Caledonia on March 27 in a bid to qualify for this summer’s World Cup.

Antonio registered 83 goals in 323 appearances for West Ham after joining from Nottingham Forest on deadline day of the 2015 summer transfer window, having largely featured out wide for Forest in the Championship.

He was an important figure in West Ham’s Conference League-winning run in the 2022-23 season, and helped the club to their best Premier League finish since 1998-99 when he recorded 10 goals and five assists in 26 league appearances during the 2020-21 campaign under David Moyes.
